title: The optimizer is now a manager

highlights.title: The optimizer is now a manager
highlights.detail: It keeps one home model running instead of trying other models to see what pays: the one you pin, or the one that has paid best on this Mac over the last 30 days. On our test Mac the old approach earned about 13–16% less than just staying on Gemma, mostly from time with no model ready. If a switch fails or no model is ready for about 10 minutes, it brings the home model back instead of switching itself off. It moves only when at least 5 Macs like yours clearly earn more on another model for 2 hours, at most 3 times a day, and stops if those moves don't pay off.

highlights.title: Fewer false alarms
highlights.detail: "Run status unavailable" no longer shows by mistake or sends problem reports on its own. Reputation shows again with Darkbloom 0.9.10, and while Darkbloom preloads at startup it shows as starting, not stopped.

highlights.title: Ratings from your own Mac
highlights.detail: Pace and day ratings are judged against this Mac's own history, with no preset earnings goal, and demand is compared with what's usual for the time of day. Statistics keep counting when your Mac offers several models, even if Darkbloom's provider list leaves out a model that isn't in its catalog.

highlights.title: Hourly bars, light mode and My Macs
highlights.detail: The Overview shows hourly $/hour bars beside the Pulse meter, with an estimate for the current hour. Choose System, Light or Dark under More → Appearance. My Macs lists every model, the pace of each, and whether the Manager is on. A one-time card in the Optimizer tab explains what changed.
